title: Chickpeas (canned, sodium added, drained and rinsed)

content.title: About
content.content: Chickpeas (Cicer arietinum) are a legume widely used in cooking. Canned chickpeas with added sodium are heat‑treated, then drained and rinsed to reduce salt content. They are ready to eat and retain most of their nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chickpeas are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown in ancient Egypt and India over 7,000 years ago.
Canned chickpeas are a convenient ingredient for quick salads, soups, and curries.
They provide about 8 g of plant protein per 100 g.
Unlike dried chickpeas, canned ones require no soaking before use.
Chickpeas belong to the legume family, along with beans, peas, and soy.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Chickpeas contain all essential amino acids, making them a valuable protein source for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs provide a steady release of glucose into the bloodstream.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B6 and folate are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: iron, magnesium, phosphorus
items.content: These minerals contribute to blood formation, muscle function, and bone health.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned chickpeas often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Chickpeas contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in very large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add chickpeas to salads, soups, stews, hummus, grain bowls, or snacks. They work well in vegetarian patties and burritos. For extra texture, lightly sauté them until crisp.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer any leftovers to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3–4 days.
